symbols.name: bit length
symbols.meaning: The rounded-up base-2 logarithm of $n$, which counts the bits of $n$.
symbols.quote: Write $b = \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ for the rounded-up base-2 logarithm of $n$, the number of bits of $n$ (the letter $b$ changes meaning here).

symbols.name: padded cell count
symbols.meaning: The number of cells of the padded box, a power of two in $[4n/b, 8n/b)$.
symbols.quote: Write $T$ for the number of cells of the padded box (the letter $T$ changes meaning here).

symbols.name: axis count
symbols.meaning: The number of axes of the padded box.
symbols.quote: Write $d = \lfloor b^{\epsilon} \rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon})$ for the number of axes of the box (the letter $d$ changes meaning here), and $K = \lfloor d^{c} \rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ for the number of bits in each address chunk, a run of consecutive address bits (the letter $K$ changes meaning here).

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each address chunk.
symbols.quote: Write $d = \lfloor b^{\epsilon} \rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon})$ for the number of axes of the box (the letter $d$ changes meaning here), and $K = \lfloor d^{c} \rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ for the number of bits in each address chunk, a run of consecutive address bits (the letter $K$ changes meaning here).

symbols.name: axis exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent with $r = 2^{\ell}$, which counts the factors of two in $r$.
symbols.quote: Write $\ell = \lceil \log_2 T/d \rceil$ for the exponent with $r = 2^{\ell}$ (the letter $\ell$ changes meaning here).

symbols.name: dimension exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed positive exponent, equal to $2^{-75}$.
symbols.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

symbols.name: chunk exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed positive exponent, equal to $2^{-56}$.
symbols.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

symbols.name: exchange exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent $1-2^{-50}$ in the cost of a chunk exchange.
symbols.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

symbols.name: round exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent $1-2^{-54}$ in the cost of a simultaneous round.
symbols.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

symbols.name: small exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed small exponent, equal to $1/16$.
symbols.quote: The fixed exponents $\epsilon = 2^{-75}$, $c = 2^{-56}$, $\tau = 1-2^{-50}$, $\lambda' = 1-2^{-54}$ and $\delta = 1/16$ are constants of the construction (the letters $c$, $\tau$ and $\delta$ change meaning here), and $\epsilon$ is not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of limit arguments.

symbols.name: line-map factor
symbols.meaning: The factor that scales the cost of the line maps.
symbols.quote: The factor $\alpha$ scales the cost of the line maps, a line being a slice of the box along one axis (the letter $\alpha$ changes meaning here).

relations.quote: The cost table splits the [running time cost](running-time-cost.md) of the algorithm into separate terms, one per kind of work.
The second row bounds the cost of the chunk exchanges that produce the [transform layout](transform-layout.md).
The first row prices moves to their [destination rank](destination-rank.md), which use $O(dK)$ linear scans.
The third row prices each simultaneous [butterfly round](transform-round.md), which acts on all axes at once.

The fourth row bounds the cost of the axis exposure and restoration around the [Chinese remainder theorem](chinese-remainder-theorem.md) step: $O(d^2)$ axis moves of cost $O(\Upsilon(1+\ell^{\tau}))$ each.
The fifth row bounds the cost of the line maps of [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md).
It divides every term by the [logical bit volume](logical-bit-volume.md) $\Upsilon$ of the box, so each term becomes a power of $p$ once $d$, $K$ and $\ell$ are substituted.
